summary: Tested scaling optimizations: Bills property-summary, Reports aggregation, Tenants pagination+search. Found and FIXED a CRITICAL backend pagination bug (missing stable secondary sort caused ~54% duplicate rows across pages — only 137/300 unique tenants). Backend 7/7 pytest pass. Frontend flows verified end-to-end on the PRO demo owner.
action_items: None required. Confirm the applied backend fix (secondary sort on `id`) is acceptable; consider adding a compound index on {user_id:1, status:1, created_at:-1, id:1} if not already covered by existing indexes.
critical_code_review_comments: list_tenants sort was `created_at desc` only — with bulk-seeded tenants sharing created_at values, MongoDB returned non-deterministic order per query, causing heavy duplication across pages (137/300 unique). Fixed by adding `id` ascending as a stable tiebreaker.
enrich() inside list_tenants issues one rent_records find per tenant (N+1). For 300+ tenants at page_size=200 this is slow. Consider a single aggregation lookup or bulk fetch by tenant_id $in.
server.py at 4777 lines — continue modularization (tenants, bills, reports).
Legacy /api/tenants (no page) returns to_list(5_000_000) — fine at current scale but risky at true scale.
context_for_next_testing_agent: New pytest file /app/backend/tests/test_scaling_endpoints.py covers bills/property-summary (current month + all), reports/summary (validates aggregate totals >300m rent, >50m bills, >20m expenses across 30 props), tenants legacy array, tenants paginated envelope (300 total / 12 pages), page-2-different (validates no duplicates), and search q=chi (35 hits). Reports response is a plain JSON LIST (not an envelope). Reports fields: expected, collected, outstanding, bills_collected, expenses_total, income, net, is_loss.
rca of the issue: BUG: /api/tenants?page=... returned overlapping items across pages. RCA: `.sort('created_at', -1).skip(...).limit(...)` — many seeded tenants share identical created_at ISO strings, so MongoDB's sort was non-deterministic; each page query returned a different arbitrary ordering of the tied documents, causing skip windows to overlap. Reproduction: fetched pages 1..12 with page_size=25 → only 137 unique of 300 expected. Mitigation: added `id` ASC as secondary sort key → verified 300 unique across all 12 pages. UI Next/Prev now shows fully disjoint pages.
